chatgpt_planning.body:
## Context
I work in IT backend/system administration. {TASK}

- Recommend an approach with trade-offs.
- List risks, prerequisites, and open questions.
- Produce a step-by-step plan I can hand to an execution agent.

{CONSTRAINTS}

1. Recommended approach (short)

workspace_agent.name: ChatGPT workspace agent design
workspace_agent.body:
Design a ChatGPT workspace agent and write its complete instructions, ready to paste. {TASK}

Most people skip the parts that make agents actually useful, so the instructions you produce MUST contain all of these sections, fully written out (not just mentioned):

1. PURPOSE & SCOPE — one sentence of purpose, an explicit out-of-scope list, allowed tools, forbidden actions.

2. MEMORY SYSTEM — the agent keeps a small set of named memory notes (e.g. 'preferences', 'project-context', 'decisions'). Rules: record only stable reusable facts; convert relative dates to absolute; durable source-of-truth files always win over memory; prune stale entries when touched. Include the exact instruction text for when to read and when to update memory.

3. SELF-REFLECTION LOOP — after each completed task the agent writes a 3-line reflection: what worked, what to reuse, what to change next time. Reflections feed memory and skills, not uncontrolled behavior changes.

4. SKILL MAKER — when the agent notices the same kind of task for the third time, it proposes a named skill: trigger, inputs, numbered steps, verification. Skills get saved and reused instead of re-deriving the workflow.

5. TASK CONTRACT — every piece of work starts with scope, inputs, constraints, outputs, and verification; the agent plans first and confirms before executing anything big.

6. VERIFICATION & HANDOFF — never claim completion without stating what was checked; if work remains, leave a handoff note with exact next steps.

7. INSTRUCTION HYGIENE — once a month (or when instructions feel bloated) the agent proposes deletions: redundant rules, stale references, conflicting guidance.

Agent purpose and context: {INPUTS}
Constraints: {CONSTRAINTS}

Output the final agent instructions as one copy-ready block, then a short note on how to test the agent with 3 sample tasks.

harness_setup.name: Harness / project setup
harness_setup.body:
Set up a working harness for this project. {TASK}

Create:
- AGENTS.md with orientation, conventions, and constraints
- A task-contract template (scope, inputs, tools, constraints, outputs, verification)
- An evidence/handoff convention

Working loop to encode:
1. Orient from nearest AGENTS.md
2. Load smallest relevant files
3. Define bounded task contract
4. Execute one coherent slice
5. Capture evidence
6. Update durable files
7. Verify before claiming completion
8. Leave a handoff

Local files are the source of truth; external systems (Jira, Confluence, SharePoint, etc.) are downstream copies.

Constraints: {CONSTRAINTS}

script_review.name: Script/code review
script_review.body:
Review this script/code before I run it in production. {TASK}

Check for:
- Destructive operations without guards or -WhatIf
- Missing error handling and silent failures
- Hardcoded credentials/values that should be parameters
- Idempotency: what happens if it runs twice
- Scope: could it touch more objects than intended

Give findings ranked by risk, with the fix for each.
Constraints: {CONSTRAINTS}

3. Anything that was ambiguous where you had to guess my intent
